data.name: Iyadi
data.gender_notes: Iyadi is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the name Iyad, which is of Arabic origin and means 'rider' or 'traveler'. In Islamic history, Iyad ibn Ghanam is known for his role as a commander and companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The name Iyadi carries the meaning “From Iyad” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Iyadi usually hope their child will grow to embody from iyad and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of a spiritual journey or travel in the path of righteousness.
data.etymology: Iyadi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “From Iyad.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iyadi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: إيادي
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من الإياد، القوة والقدرة على فعل الشيء
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم إيادي مشتق من الجذر العربي 'أي د' والذي يحمل معاني القوة والقدرة على فعل الشيء. يدل على الشخص القوي والقدر على الإتيان بالأفعال الحسنة. ورد في بعض التفاسير القرآنية أن الإياد هو القيام بالشيء على وجه الإتقان والإحسان.

in_urdu.name: ایادی
in_urdu.meaning: طاقت اور صلاحیت رکھنے والا، مضبوط اور قابل شخص
in_urdu.long_meaning: ایادی نام عربی جڑ 'أي د' سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے طاقت اور صلاحیت۔ یہ نام ان شخصیتوں کو مخاطب کرتا ہے جو مضبوط، قابل اور اہل ہیں۔ اسلامی تقالید میں اس نام کی اہمیت اس کی عربی اصل اور روحانی مضمرات کی وجہ سے ہے۔

in_hindi.name: इयादी
in_hindi.meaning: शक्ति और योग्यता रखने वाला, मजबूत और सक्षम व्यक्ति
in_hindi.long_meaning: इयादी नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल 'أي د' से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है शक्ति और योग्यता। यह नाम उन व्यक्तित्वों को संबोधित करता है जो मजबूत, सक्षम और योग्य हैं। भारतीय मुस्लिम परंपरा में इस नाम का महत्व इसकी अरबी उत्पत्ति और आध्यात्मिक महत्व के कारण है।

in_pashto.name: ایادي
in_pashto.meaning: ځواکمن او وړ شخص، مضبوط او پياوړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ایادي نوم د عربي ريښو 'أي د' څخه اخيستل شوی دی، کوم چې د ځواک او وړتيا معنی لري. دا نوم هغو کسانو ته خطاب کوي چي قوي، وړ او پياوړي دي. په افغان او پښتون دود کې ددې نوم اهميت د هغې عربي اصل او روحاني معنا له امله دی.

in_english.name: Iyadi
in_english.meaning: Strong and capable person, empowered with good deeds
in_english.long_meaning: The name Iyadi originates from the Arabic root 'أي د' (Ay-D), which signifies strength, capability, and the power to perform actions with excellence. In Islamic tradition, Iyadi connotes a person who is strong, capable, and proficient in good deeds. The etymology of Iyadi relates to the concept of 'Iyad' in Arabic, which implies the act of supporting or strengthening something. This name is not directly mentioned in the Quran but is derived from roots that reflect positive attributes valued in Islamic culture. Historically, names like Iyadi have been used to express aspirations for a child's character and abilities. Spiritually, Iyadi suggests a personality that is resilient, resourceful, and dedicated to righteous actions.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hadid, Tarikh al-Islam wa Wafayat al-Muluk. Iyadid al-Andalusi served as the last Umayyad governor of Granada from 1482 to 1492. During his rule, he attempted to maintain the Islamic presence in Spain by strengthening fortifications and diplomatic relations with European powers, but ultimately failed to prevent the fall of Granada to the Christian forces led by Ferdinand and Isabella in 1492.

Ibn Khaldun, Al-'Ibar. Iyad ibn Musa al-Ya'qubi was an Andalusian historian who wrote a comprehensive history of the Islamic world from its beginnings to his own time. His work, Al-Khansa al-kabira (The Major Work), was completed around 1377 and is considered one of the most important sources for understanding the history of the Islamic West (al-Maghrib).
